overall: The AG found the Brockton Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to give the public adequate access to its October 7, 2015 meeting, and found no violation on the other alleged issues.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly deliberated on a draft peer review contract immediately after its Sept 1, 2015 meeting and outside a meeting before the Sept 16 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to find a violation because the Board took prompt action to reconvene the meeting in an effort to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: At its Sept 16, 2015 meeting the Board allegedly discussed two topics (a lot release and a covenant release) not listed on the posted notice.
Members of the public allegedly could not hear the Board's discussion at the Sept 16, 2015 meeting held in a substitute conference room.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, absent any other evidence to the contrary, we credit the Board's assertion that the audience could hear its deliberations during this meeting.

allegations.summary: At the Oct 7, 2015 meeting on the power plant, the Board allegedly failed to accommodate all attendees, leaving some standing in the hallway without access or video.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide the public with adequate access to its October 7, 2015 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint named three individuals who are public officials but not members of the Board; the AG declined to review allegations against them.
allegations.key_passage: These individuals are public officials who are not members of a public body, thus they are not subject to the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
